findings.title: CRLF Injection in HTTP Headers
findings.description: The fix correctly adds \Z anchors to prevent regex injection. In the old code, the $ anchor allows \n to bypass validation. An attacker could inject CRLF sequences (\r\n) into HTTP headers, leading to HTTP response splitting or header injection vulnerabilities. This is a critical security vulnerability as it allows bypassing input validation for HTTP headers.
findings.suggestion: The fix is correct. Ensure all code paths using these validators apply them to user-controlled header names and values before sending requests. Verify that the validators are consistently applied across all HTTP request construction methods (GET, POST, etc.) to prevent CRLF injection.
